Isn´t "Wake" a better card than "Forced" always? Or am I missing something?

Wake with Evening's Freshness

Do not replace until your next untap phase.
Only usable by a tapped vampire. This reacting vampire can play reaction cards and attempt to block as though untapped until the current action is concluded.

Forced Awakening

Messages.Author: jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
> Rollingthunder wrote:
> Isn´t "Wake" a better card than "Forced" always? Or am I missing something?
They're both good cards.

Wake with Evening's Freshness's major downside is that you do not replace it until your next untap phase.  If you play it, you don't cycle into a new card. It reduces your hand size all the way until your next turn, in a game where cardflow is really important.

When you play Forced Awakening, you get to draw a replacement immediately. That can be hugely important.  If you fail to block (or choose not to block), then you burn a blood, so Forced Awakening is generally better when you have some intercept.  But sometimes, you can play Forced Awakening and immediately replace it with that Deflection that's going to save you.  So you'll sacrifice the extra blood to stay alive.

It is usually a good idea to mix up the types of "Wake Cards" in your deck, due to some being situationally better than others; also just in case someone plays Direct Intervention on your first Wake (i.e. WWEF), you can play a different one (like FA).

Also, WWEF and FA are also just 2 of many "Wake Effect" cards.. On the Qui Vive, Eyes of Argus, etc..

And there are also the slightly-different "Untap as a reaction" cards like Guard Dogs, 2nd Tradition, Black Sunrise,...

Just be careful to read the card text of each card to see what its restrictions are (such as forcing you to attempt to block, or no-replace, or once-per-turn, etc etc).

Also, I like to have a few different type of wake-cards in my deck. The choice depends on the type of the deck and metagame and the draw-back of the given reaction card.
On the Qui vive: only one per minion between his/her two untap phases, but usable by an ally.
Wake with evening's freshness: the 'do not replace' clause can be annoying
Forced Awakening: less useful if you plan to stealth-bump a bleed to deflect it afterwards
Eluding the Arms of Morpheus: in most cases this will leave you untapped if the block attempt did not succeed.

Messages.Author: HenricF
Messages.Body:
For me, it depends on the type of deck I'm using. For example, I have one Tremere/!Tremere wall deck that usually performs at least decent in our games. The deck is built around intercept, provided by vampires such as Carna and library cards such as Bowl of Convergence, Sport Bike, Enhanced Senses and several +1 intercept cards. Thus, I don't expect to fail blocks very often and the deck includes more Forced Awakening than WwEF:s.

In other decks, with smaller chances of successfully blocking, I'd include less Forced Awakenings and more WwEF and OtQv.
